decision_maker: Service Director (Education and Skills) (Claire Hayes)
purpose:
Oak Grove College is a
secondary special school in Worthing offering generic Special
Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) provision for children
and young people aged between 11 and 19. There is a need to
increase the number of places at the College and a feasibility
study and initial design work has been undertaken to enable this
increase by the establishment of a satellite provision to Oak Grove
on another site owned by the County Council. The study has
illustrated how the building and site at The Pines, Worthing, if
established as a satellite site, could expand the pupil places for
Oak Grove by up to 60 taking the current planned places from 278 to
338.
 
The 
Department for Education (DfE) guidance sets out the process
that should be undertaken when considering expanding a special
school which consists of a number of stages.  An 
informal consultation was launched in Spring 2025 to seek views
on the proposal to create a satellite site for Oak Grove College.
The consultation ran during April and May 2025 and views and
comments were collated from interested parties
 
After considering the feedback
from the consultation, which indicated that over 95% of those who
responded supported the proposal, in September 2025 the Cabinet
Member for Children, Young People and Learning 
approved progression to the next stage of the DfE process, the
publication of formal statutory proposals to create an additional
60 places for Oak Grove College at a satellite site at The Pines.
The Cabinet Member also delegated authority to the Service Director
(Education and Skills) to determine whether the proposal should
proceed following consideration of any representations received
during the statutory consultation stage.
 
The 
Statutory Proposals were published for a four-week period
during October and November 2025 and this provided the opportunity
for all interested parties and the public to submit any comments
about the proposal.
 
96.1% of those who responded
supported the expansion and further details of the representations
received during the statutory proposal period are set out in
section 4 of this report. Following consideration of the
representations received it is proposed to proceed with the
creation of a satellite site at The Pines for Oak Grove
College.

decision_maker: Service Director (Education and Skills) (Claire Hayes)
purpose:
St Anthony’s is a special
school in Chichester offering Special Educational Needs and
Disabilities (SEND) provision for children and young people with
moderate learning difficulties aged between 4 and 16. There is a
need to increase the number of places at the school to meet rising
demand. A feasibility study and initial design work has been
undertaken to expand St Anthony’s into vacant school
buildings situated on the same site as the special school (these
were previously occupied by Jessie Younghusband Primary School). St
Anthony’s expansion into these school buildings would create
up to 50 additional specialist school places, increasing St
Anthony’s planned place numbers from 264 to 314.
 
The 
Department for Education (DfE) guidance sets out the process
that should be undertaken when considering expanding a special
school which consists of a number of stages.  In December 2023 
approval was given to launch an 
initial public consultation to seek views on the proposal to
relocate Jessie Younghusband from its shared site with St
Anthony’s School, to a new primary school on the housing
development west of Chichester, known as Minerva Heights. As part
of that consultation views were also sought on the proposal to
expand St Anthony’s into the Jessie Younghusband Primary
School site once vacated. The process related to the relocation of
Jessie Younghusband school progressed with the move to the new
school buildings happening to enable opening on the new school site
in September 2025.
 
After considering the feedback
from the consultation relating to expanding
St Anthony’s in September 2025, the Cabinet Member for
Children, Young People and Learning 
approved progression to the next stage of the DfE process, the
publication of formal statutory proposals to expand the school by
50 places. The Cabinet Member also delegated authority to the
Service Director (Education and Skills) to determine whether the
proposal should proceed following consideration of any
representations received during the statutory consultation
stage.
 
The 
statutory proposals were published for a four-week period
during October and November 2025 and this provided the opportunity
for all interested parties and the public to submit any comments
about the expansion proposal.
 
94.7% of those who responded
supported the expansion and further details of the representations
received during the statutory proposal period are set out in
section 4 of this report.  Following
consideration of the representations received it is proposed to
proceed with the expansion of St Anthony’s School.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Performance and Resources
Report (PRR) details the Council’s position in relation to
revenue and capital spending, budget planning, workforce
projections, performance and risk management by portfolio against
the County Council’s priorities.  The Leader, Cabinet Member for Finance &
Property, or Cabinet will be recommended to approve the PRR and any
decisions required in relation to budget (revenue or capital),
resources and performance management.
content:
The Performance and Resources
Report (PRR) details the Council’s position in relation to
revenue and capital spending, budget planning, workforce
projections, performance and risk management by portfolio against
the County Council’s priorities.  The Leader, Cabinet Member for Finance &
Property, or Cabinet will be recommended to approve the PRR and any
decisions required in relation to budget (revenue or capital),
resources and performance management.

Following
consideration of the report the Cabinet resolved:
1.  
To note the financial challenges set out in paragraphs 1.3 –
1.24.
2.  
To approve the overall revenue and capital financial outturn
position within the Performance and Resources Report including:

a.   
Agreeing the overall revenue outturn overspend position of
£12.976m, which is made up of the following items:

                               
i.      
Overspending of Portfolio Budgets of £30.232m,

                              
ii.      
Additional Financing Income received of £5.163m, and

                            
iii.      
A mix of additional funding and unspent budget within Non-Portfolio
Budgets of £12.093m.

b.   
Agreeing the allocation of the £9.964m of General Contingency
budget to the overall revenue outturn overspend position.

c.   
Noting the required draw-down of £6.0m from the Social Care
Reserve and £6.976m from the Budget Management Reserve.
The call-in deadline is 9 July 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the overall revenue and capital financial outturn position, addressing an overspend of £12.976m.

decision_maker: Service Director (Property and Assets) (Andrew Edwards)
purpose:
The Weald School is a co-educational secondary
school with a sixth form situated in Billingshurst, West Sussex. It
caters for around 1700 pupils in years 7-13 including its sixth
form.
 
The school has an under-used canteen and part
of it is currently being utilised as a very basic dance studio. It
is proposed that S106 developer contributions, that are for
specific use at The Weald School, fund the demolition of the
canteen and replacement with an activity studio, repurposed rooms
and a new build consisting of ICT Suite, and ancillary spaces.
 
Authority is now sought to allocate this S106
funding to deliver the refurbishments and improvements, which would
benefit the school and pupils.

decision_maker: Leader (Cllr Jay Mercer)
purpose:
During 2025 West
Sussex County Council worked with West Sussex districts and
boroughs to develop shared proposals for local government
reorganisation in the county, submitting preferences to Government
in September 2025.These are set out in decision 
CAB04 (25/26).
On 25 March
2026, the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local
Government, Rt Hon Steve Reed OBE MP, 
wrote to the leaders of West Sussex councils to inform
them that he has not yet made a decision about
the proposals for West Sussex. 
The Secretary of
State set out the rationale for this in his
letter, noting that he is considering modifications
that may address his concerns, which the department would run a
technical consultation on after the county elections in May
2026.  The modification for West Sussex
was to the two unitary proposal – moving Chichester from the
proposed council with Adur, Arun and Worthing to the proposed
council with Crawley, Horsham and Mid Sussex.
The Government
has opened a consultation (Modified
proposals for local government reorganisation in West Sussex -
GOV.UK) - running to 15 June 2026 - seeking the views of
West Sussex councils and other named consultees on the modified
approach.
The Government is seeking views on if the potential modification
to the two unitary proposal is better than the original two unitary
proposal contained in the West Sussex business case.
Due to the need for this matter
to be determined as soon as possible the Leader has secured
agreement from the Chair of the County Council for this key
decision to be taken without prior notice in the Forward Plan of
key decisions (Part 4, Section 1, Standing Order 3.62) (Regulation
11) because delay would prejudice the County Council’s
interests.

content:

The Committee considered a report by the Executive Director of Law,
Assurance and Insight on two changes to the Constitution for
recommendation to the County Council: firstly, to clarify the rules
in Standing Orders relating to points of order and personal
explanation; and secondly, to change overarching responsibility for
the production of the Annual Governance Statement from the
Regulation, Audit and Accounts Committee (RAAC) to the Governance
Committee (copy appended to the signed minutes).

 
4.2       
The Executive Director of Law, Assurance and Insight commented that
the change in relation to the Annual Governance Statement will give
the Governance Committee the role of developing the Statement and
monitoring the action plan, in line with its responsibility for the
Council’s governance arrangements, but that RAAC will still
see the Statement as part of the annual accounts process.
 
4.3       
Cllr Dennis, a former Chair of RAAC, expressed support for the
proposal as although the Annual Governance Statement is part of the
consideration of the annual statement of accounts, it makes more
sense for it to be the responsibility of the Governance
Committee.
 
4.4       
Resolved –
 

That the following changes to the Constitution be endorsed for
recommendation to the County Council in July:
 
(1)        
Amendments to Standing Orders clarifying the rules relating to
points of order and of personal explanation, as set out at
paragraph 2.1 of the report; and
 
(2)        
Amendments to the terms of reference of the Governance and
Regulation, Audit and Accounts Committees, relating to the Annual
Governance Statement, as set out in Appendix 1 to the report.
topline: The County Council has decided to clarify rules on points of order and change responsibility for the Annual Governance Statement

decision_maker: Service Director (Property and Assets) (Andrew Edwards)
purpose:
Portfield Primary Academy is a primary school
based in the Chichester area that is part of The Kemnal Academies
Trust (TKAT) Multi Academy Trust.
 
Due to increased house building in the
Chichester area, and the consequent rise in pupil numbers at
Portfield Primary, the School and Academy Trust approached the
Local Authority to submit a request for funding from the Community
Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would enable an expansion project
to be undertaken delivering additional classrooms and ancillary
spaces at the school.
 
The request for CIL funding has been approved
and, as part of the agreement with Chichester District Council, the
CIL funds will be paid directly to the County Council who will then
transfer the payments in instalments on to the Academy Trust
enabling the expansion project to be progressed.

decision_maker: Service Director (Highways, Transport and Planning) (Matt Davey)
content:
The Service Director (Highways, Transport
and Planning) has approved funding for applications submitted to
the West Sussex Lane Rental Surplus Fund (WSLRSF) for May as
follows:
WSLRSF8 - Funding is for the completion
of the remaining northern sections of the Centurion Way which aims
to expand the low carbon/active travel opportunities in the local
area, including enabling new circular routes, with associated
wellbeing benefits and benefits to the local economy. Upon its
completion it will link the South Downs Way at Cocking and the
wider Bridleway network at Hoefield Lane. The value of the
application is £200,000.
WSLRSF19 - The application is for
Southern Gas Networks (SGN) to replace legacy percussive barholing
with a precision, insulated drilling method and capture drilling
dust at source. This is to finish investigations faster, disturb
the highway less and materially improve health outcomes for
engineers and the public. The value of the application is
£148,020.
WSLRSF24 - The project aims to trial a
range of practical interventions designed to mitigate, reduce or
deter abusive behaviour towards workers operating on the highway
network. These interventions include site-wide CCTV coverage, clear
“CCTV in Operation” signage, Heras fencing with plain
screening to provide increased shielding and separation and Heras
fencing with printed imagery or behavioural messaging aimed at
influencing driver and public conduct. The purpose of the trials is
to evaluate the effectiveness of different combinations of physical
and visual interventions in reducing abusive and unacceptable
behaviour. The value of the application is £75,000.
topline: The Service Director (Highways, Transport and Planning) has decided to approve funding for projects including completing Centurion Way and trialing interventions to reduce abusive behavior towards workers on the highway network.

decision_maker: Service Director (Property and Assets) (Andrew Edwards)
purpose:
North Mundham School is a 210
place, 7 class school for children aged 4-11 years old. The school
consists of a broad range of buildings including a double modular
unit which was installed more than 30 years ago and has been
identified as requiring replacement due to its age and significant
condition issues.
 
Projections indicate that the
60 pupil places currently accommodated in the modular block are
required to ensure continued capacity for children of primary age
in the village and wider locality. 
Without pupil places West Sussex County Council will be unable to
meet its statutory duties to ensure sufficient school places in
this area.
 
In January 2025 approval was
provided for the allocation of funds to replace the life expired
double modular unit with two new classrooms and to carry out
associated works such as landscaping (decision 
CYPL21(24/25) refers).
 
A competitive tender exercise
was undertaken in Autumn 2025, resulting in a contract being
awarded to undertake the project. However, this contract was
terminated by WSCC in April 2026 due to the contractor’s
non-performance.
 
Due to the increasingly
dilapidated state of the modular unit, there is a risk of it being
condemned and unfit for use. This means progressing the
construction works in delivering replacement accommodation is
becoming more urgent. Therefore, instead of undertaking a further
tender exercise it is proposed to directly award the contract for
the construction works to replace the modular accommodation at
North Mundham Primary School to an alternative
contractor.

purpose:

Accommodation and Support for Older Children We Care For and Care Leavers (the Framework), which enables

provider.
 
The Framework was

extend for up to a further two years.

sufficiency, quality and value for money. Approval is now sought to
exercise the option to extend the Framework for the remaining two
years from September 2026.
 
The agreed initial period of
the Framework was 5 years, with the potential to extend the
Framework for up to a further 2 years. 
The Framework is operating successfully, and it is proposed to seek
agreement to extend the framework for the remaining two
years.

decision_maker: Service Director (Education and Skills) (Claire Hayes)
purpose:
The County Council 
commissions Chichester College Group to deliver a unique
education provision for pupils aged 14-16 whose needs are deemed
better met by a more vocational curriculum.
 
The package of provision is known as
‘Freshstart’ and is delivered across selected campuses
constituting the Chichester College Group (CCG).
 
Building on the success of the service to date
it is proposed to continue to commission CCG to continue offering
this provision until July 2028. This style of provision for
selected Key Stage 4 learners in such a further education setting
provides a variable package of core, vocational and enrichment
education at an appropriate level. Individual packages are tailored
to best suit the academic, social and emotional needs of each
learner in order to achieve and maximise positive progression
post-Key Stage 4 (KS4).

decision_maker: Service Director (Property and Assets) (Andrew Edwards)
purpose:
Imberhorne School in East Grinstead
is one of two secondary schools for pupils aged 11-18 serving the
East Grinstead locality. The school operates over two sites with
the Lower School (for Years 7 to 9) on a site at Windmill Lane and
the Upper School (for Years 10 to 13) on a site at Imberhorne Lane.
 
The Lower School site at
Windmill Lane, which currently caters for 826 pupils, has
significant condition and suitability issues particularly in
relation to pupil toilets and also the modular teaching
accommodation, which is now in excess of 30 years old. In order to
address this £2.835m of Section 106 (S106) developer
contributions, that are specified for use for education
infrastructure works at Imberhorne
School, were 
approved to undertake a priority scheme of improvement works at
the Lower School.
 
Following completion of a
feasibility study to assess the scope of a wider programme of works
and a review of S106 funds available, approval is now sought to
increase the overall funding available for a programme of
investment at Imberhorne School. It is
proposed that works are delivered in phases by the school,
undertaken as School Managed Projects, with passporting of funds to
the school as design and works progress.

purpose:
The Council has a legal obligation to make
provisions for a Free School Meals (FSM) service for Local
Education Authority (LEA) schools, or a process to make available
to schools a FSM service. The Council
meets this obligation by managing a Framework of catering providers
appointed through a competitive tender exercise. Whilst it is not a
legal obligation the Council also expects the provision of a
student paid meal service to be offered as part of these
contracts.
 
The existing contract, initially let in 2018,
for the provision of a Secondary School Catering Service Provider
Framework in West Sussex, came to an end on 31 May 2025. The
Framework contract had been fully extended to its permissible total
contract length of 7 years. The combined school contracts awarded
from the Framework are currently worth approximately £1.94m
per annum, with the contract cost for each school being funded by
that school.  Approval is therefore
sought to commence a procurement process to establish a new
framework that enables the sourcing of future secondary school
meals contracts.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Economy and Skills (Cllr Garry Wall)
purpose:
West Sussex County
Council’s Adult Learning Service, situated within the
Communities Directorate, commissions and delivers adult skills and
learning provision funded primarily through grant allocations from
the Department for Education and the Department for Work and
Pensions, alongside other current and future government funding
streams and initiatives.
 
The Council currently operates
an Adult Learning and Skills Framework, established in 2024, to
support commissioning across a range of programmes including Adult
Skills Fund provision, Free Courses for Jobs, Skills Bootcamps,
Tailored Learning and 16 to 19 Study Programmes.
 
West Sussex County Council has
been invited to participate in the Government’s Pathway to
Devolution pilot for Academic Year 2026/27. The pilot is intended
to support transition towards devolved Adult Skills Fund
responsibilities and provides additional formula-funded allocation
of monies for delivery to participating Local
Authorities.
 
East Sussex County Council and
Brighton & Hove City Council have also indicated their
intention to participate in the pilot and have requested support
from West Sussex Adult Learning Service to access a compliant route
to market to support commissioning of provision. The existing West
Sussex Framework does not permit access by partner authorities
therefore authority is sought to commence a procurement process to
establish a new Framework that could be utilised pan-Sussex for the
commissioning of Adult Learning and Skills.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways and Transport (Cllr Joy Dennis)
purpose:
As part of West Sussex County
Council’s Active Travel Fund (ATF) programme, a scheme was
submitted within one of its primary objectives to enhance the
cycling and walking provisions along West Parade and North
Parade.
 
Following confirmation of the
bid’s success, work proceeded on taking the scheme through
the design stages. This resulted in a proposal comprising of the
introduction of a cycle contraflow running west to east along the
length of West Parade, a speed limit reduction, weight limit
restriction and two new signalised crossing points, one to replace
the existing island refuge on Wimblehurst Road, the other on the
southern arm of the North Parade/Hurst Road junction (Appendix
A).
 
The initial proposal was
distributed to the local area with a drop-in event held in June
2025 to gauge public opinion and wants with the foremost issue
being the loss of parking spaces on the eastern end of West Parade.
The design was consequently amended to reduce the number of spaces
lost and sent for public consultation in February 2026.  The proposal was supported prior to consultation
by both Councillor Nigel Dennis and Councillor Andrew Baldwin.
Sussex Police were consulted and expressed no concerns or
objections to the proposal.
 
The consultation received 16
formal objections from members of the public which included 12
representations.

initiation of the Implementation and Delivery Phase of the
Council’s Early Support Programme. This phase forms a core
element of the Connected Council transformation agenda,
which seeks to improve outcomes and manage rising demand
through strengthened integration and preventative
approaches. 
 
The Implementation and Delivery
Phase will progress the recommendations arising from the diagnostic
work and undertake further system-wide activity across Adult Social
Care, Children’s Services, and the wider community network.
Engagement will continue with key partners, including health
services, District and Borough Councils, and the Voluntary,
Community and Social Enterprise (VCSE) sector, to ensure a
coordinated and collaborative approach. 
 
This phase will focus

recommendations, enhancing system-wide coordination, and developing
more effective and sustainable models of support. To enable
delivery, the Council may commission specialist consultancy support
where this is deemed necessary. Any external
partner(s) would be
required to demonstrate substantial experience in
leading complex transformation within public sector systems,
particularly across health and social care. Where appointed, the
partner would support implementation in the following
areas: 
 

Early
intervention 


Prevention 


Cross?system
collaboration involving Adult Social Care, Children’s
Services, health partners, VCSE organisations, and District and
Borough Councils 

  
The Cabinet Member
for Adults Services will be asked to approve the
commencement of work required for the Implementation and
Delivery Phase. This may include approval
to procure external consultancy support should it
be deemed necessary, and delegation for the Executive
Director of Adults’ Services and Health (DASS) to award any
related contract(s).

Sussex County Council (WSCC) and Crawley Borough Council (CBC),
with WSCC acting as the accountable body.  The programme supports sustainable economic growth
development and investment, with the County Council’s total
capital commitment being £19.171m over the life of the
CGP.

Improvement Scheme is one of the core components of the CGP,
intended to modernise one of the region’s busiest transport
hubs through enhancements to the station forecourt, improved
transport interchange arrangements, better accessibility, and
support for sustainable travel.
 
Sustained construction
inflation and adjustments to the scheme since it was originally
proposed have led to an increase in the cost estimate to deliver
the project.  However, underspends
within the wider CGP mean that the Three Bridges scheme can still
be delivered within the overall approved Crawley Growth Programme
funding envelope.
 
Approval is sought to
reallocate funding within the Crawley Growth Programme to meet the
updated cost requirement. Agreement is also sought to authorise the
drawdown and transfer of the necessary capital allocation to
Crawley Borough Council, enabling scheme delivery in accordance
with established governance and partnership arrangements

for the introduction of the Crisis and Resilience Fund from
1st April 2026. This new 3-year grant introduces a shift
from reacting to crises to preventing them, aiming to strengthen
local support through a joined-up, holistic approach. It combines
emergency assistance with preventative measures to build financial
resilience among households and communities.
 
This key decision will ask the
Cabinet Member for Community Support, Fire and Rescue to receive
the allocation of grant funding for 3 years (2026 – 2029) and
delegate authority of the distribution of funds, within the
parameters set out in the grant determination letter, to the
Executive Director of Communities.
 
It is noted that any Award of
Contracts over £1m will require a further key decision and
any contracts awarded under this threshold will be subject to a
non-key decision. Any further Crisis and resilience fund grant
receipts will be publicly reported through the council’s
Performance and Resources Report.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
Palatine Primary School is a
Special School in Worthing offering provision for children with
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). The school
offers generic SEND provision for those aged between 4 and
11.
 
There is a need to increase the
number of places at the school. A feasibility study and initial
design work have been undertaken to enable this increase by the
establishment of a satellite provision to Palatine Primary School
on another site owned by the County Council. The study has
illustrated how the building and site at Lyndhurst Infant School,
if established as a satellite site, could accommodate a total of 75
places.  This would be made up of 41
additional specialist school places and, to address overcapacity at
the main Palatine school site, reduce the number of pupils
accommodated there by 34 to 190. This would increase the
school’s overall planned place numbers to 262.
 

Approval was given to commence an 
initial consultation in accordance with 
Department for Education (DfE) guidance, to seek views on the
proposal to create a satellite site for Palatine Primary School.
The 
consultation ran during September and October 2025. Views and
comments have been collated from interested parties. Details of the
consultation and the feedback received are set out in section 4 of
this report.
 
The DfE guidance sets out the
stages of the process that should be undertaken when considering
expanding, by establishing a satellite site to a school. Having
completed the first stage, the initial consultation, the Cabinet
Member is now asked to consider the feedback received and consider
whether to approve the progression of the proposal to the next
stage of the process – publication of statutory
notices.
 
Adaptations would be required
to the Lyndhurst Infant site to enable creation of the satellite
site; therefore, approval is also sought for allocating the capital
funding required to finalise the design and enable delivery of the
satellite site, should it be determined this proposal should
proceed.

through provision of a capped grant.

required capital funding to finalise the design and enable delivery
of this new residential facility.

decision_maker: Executive Director of Children, Young People and Learning (Daniel Ruaux)
purpose:
The Urgent and Specialist
Support Framework 
was established in March 2022 and enables the County Council to
commission providers to deliver care, support and supervision to
some of the most vulnerable children and young people. These
packages of care may be based in family homes, community or
residential settings, hospitals and occasionally rented
accommodation. The types of packages required range from a few
hours 1:1 care to 24hrs constant supervision to support children
with mental ill-health, disabilities, placement or family
breakdowns and mother and baby supervision.
 
The 
agreed initial period of the Framework was 4 years, with the
potential for a further 4-year extension. The Framework has proved
successful in enabling a diverse range of support to be delivered
and has resulted in more packages of support for children than
originally envisaged. As a result, there has been a much higher
spend against the framework than originally projected removing the
potential option to extend the Framework beyond the initial
period.
 
Commissioning urgent and
specialist support through the existing providers on the Framework
has worked well in delivering the right care packages for these
vulnerable children and young people. 
Therefore, to ensure this can continue, it is proposed to direct
award contracts to the current providers for a two-year period.
This will provide time to review requirements for future
commissioning and launch a procurement to secure provision on
conclusion of these contracts.

purpose:
The County Council has a statutory duty to
provide sufficient school places for all children who need a place.
The demand for places for children with Special Educational Needs
and Disability (SEND), has been increasing significantly. To
support this increase, the County Council has prioritised creating
additional places through expanding existing Special Support
Centres (SSCs) or establishing new SSCs, to support children with
specific needs in a mainstream setting. This will also prevent the
need for costly provision for these children through placements in
independent and non-maintained special schools.
 
Buckingham Park Primary is a Primary School in
Shoreham by Sea and, in response to the falling demand for places,
with effect from September 2025, has reduced its Published
Admission Number (PAN) from 90 to 60 places per year. The school
has been identified as a suitable site to host a new SSC, providing
specialist support for initially twelve children aged 4–11
years of age with social communication needs/differences. The
proposal is to refurbish and remodel existing surplus space within
Buckingham Park Primary School to create the SSC.
 

Approval was provided to launch an initial public consultation,
in accordance with 
Department for Education (DfE) guidance, to seek views on the
proposal to create the SSC in part of the surplus accommodation.
The 
consultation ran during September and October 2025. Views and
comments have been collated from interested parties. Details of the
consultation and the feedback received are set out in section 4 of
this report.
 
The DfE guidance sets out the stages of the
process that should be undertaken when considering creating a new
SSC at a school. Having completed the first stage, the initial
consultation, the Cabinet Member is now asked to consider the
feedback received and consider whether to approve the progression
of the proposal to the next stage of the process –
publication of statutory notices.

having to access acute settings.

Services is asked to agree the commencement of the procurement and
delegate the award of contract(s) to the Executive Director
Adults’ Services and Health.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Environment and Climate Change (Cllr Deborah Urquhart)
purpose:
In
December 2025 and January 2026, forty shipping containers were lost
overboard in two separate incidents off the West Sussex coastline,
resulting in significant shoreline pollution from ruptured
containers and widespread debris. West Sussex County Council,
working with district and borough councils and supported by HM
Coastguard, activated a coordinated multi-agency emergency response
to protect public safety, the environment, and local
infrastructure.
Under the pre-existing Sussex Coastal Pollution Clean-up &
Disposal Service Framework, Ambipar, a specialist pollution
contractor, was deployed immediately to lead shoreline recovery,
waste handling, and clean-up operations. Temporary depots were
established, daily monitoring and recovery teams were mobilised to
remove debris, including collaboration with heavy?lifting
contractors recovering container remnants. A phased demobilisation
is underway, once the shoreline was restored as far as reasonably
practicable.
Due to the need for this matter
to be determined as soon as possible the decision maker has advised
the appropriate Scrutiny Chairman that this key decision will be
taken with limited notice in the Forward Plan of key decisions
(Part 4, Section 1, Standing Order 3.56) (Regulation 10) because
delay would prejudice the County Council’s
interests.

purpose:
The City of Chichester, the County town of
West Sussex, attracts large numbers of visitors each year due to
its historical and national importance. As a major regional centre
of administration, retail and cultural facilities Chichester plays
an important role in the region.
 
The existing pedestrianised zones in North and
East Street, laid with red brick paviours and York stone slabs in
the 1970s, have deteriorated and require major intervention and
investment.  Alongside upgrading the
surface of these pedestrianised zones, it was recognised there was
opportunity to undertake a wider initiative aimed at fostering
growth, attracting further inward investment, and enhancing the
city's appeal and safety for residents, visitors, and businesses.
This aligns with the aims of the 
Chichester Growth Deal, a key partnership with Chichester
District Council, which identified Public Realm Improvements in the
city centre as a priority to boost the local economy.
 
In October 2024, 
approval was given to allocate funding for undertaking design
work to develop an improvement scheme for the city and undertake
public engagement to inform the design.
 
Following on from this engagement a final
design for the improvement scheme has now been developed.
Therefore, authority is sought for the allocation of the funding
required to complete the design work and launch a procurement
process to deliver the final construction phase of the scheme as
set out in section 2 of the report.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
Twineham CE (Voluntary Controlled)
Primary School is a Church of England school located in the village
of Twineham, to the West of Burgess
Hill, and South-West of Haywards Heath. 
The school caters for children aged 4 – 11 with a capacity
for 105 pupils with up to 15 pupils in each year group.  The demand for places at the school has been
declining over time with 66 pupils on roll in the autumn term 2023,
48 pupils on roll in the autumn term of 2024, and 13 pupils on roll
in the spring term of 2026.  This
continued decline in numbers has led to concerns about the
viability of the school.
 
The 
DfE guidance sets out the
stages of the process that should be undertaken when considering a
closure of a rural school.  In September
2025, the Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning
approved the launch of a public consultation to seek views on the
proposal to close the school from 31st August
2026 (decision
CYPL07(25/26) refers).  After
considering the feedback from the consultation, the Cabinet Member
approved progression to the next stage of the DfE process, the
publication of formal statutory proposals to discontinue the school
(decision
CYPL20 (25/26) refers). The statutory proposals were published
for a five-week period from 22nd January to 26th February 2026 and
this provided the opportunity for all interested parties and the
public to submit any comments about the proposals for
discontinuance.
 
Details of representations received during the statutory
proposal period are set out in sections 4 and 5 of this
report.  Following consideration of the
representations received it is proposed to proceed with the
closure.

purpose:

young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND)
who are accessing education at special schools in West Sussex,
mirroring the national trend. All young people attending special
schools have an education health and care plan (EHCP) which
outlines their needs, specifies provision of support and goals and
ensures a child’s requirements are met in a holistic way. The
plan outlines defined education, health and social care
provision.

identified in EHCP’s. The SaLT

via a section 75 agreement (a form of partnership agreement with
the NHS using pooled funds) which has now ceased resulting in the
County Council needing to put its own contract in place. The
intention is to allocate additional funds to enable the expansion
of the service to include all grant maintained special schools and
to offer provision for Special Support Centres. 
 
Approval is now sought for the County Council
to establish the necessary commissioning arrangements to enable the
continued delivery of a speech and language therapy service for
schools.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Fire and Rescue National
Framework for England (2018) requires all Fire and Rescue
Authorities to produce a Community Risk Management Plan (CRMP) that
covers at least a 3-year period.
 
West Sussex Fire and Rescue
Service (WSFRS) are now in the fourth and final year of our
existing 2022 - 2026 CRMP and have developed a new CRMP covering
the period of 2026 - 2030.
 
During the planning process, we
consider our community risks, using a range of sophisticated
analytical tools to identify where incidents might happen, when
they might occur and how serious they could be. Using this data
alongside historical information about demand allows us to identify
options to better target our resources, including firefighters and
appliances, more effectively, resulting in a better balance of
prevention, protection and response activities.
 
This plan then clearly
communicates this to the public, reinforcing the services
commitment to our communities.
 
The Cabinet is recommended to
endorse the West Sussex Fire and Rescue Service Community Risk
Management Plan for 2026 - 2030 on behalf of the County
Council.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways and Transport (Cllr Joy Dennis)
purpose:
Delivery of Phase 1A Barnham
Road Roundabout on the 
A29 realignment scheme is dependent on land purchase or land
being dedicated for highways use. 
Discussions with the landowners and developers of the adjacent
housing schemes and their representatives are ongoing but there is
a risk that agreement may not be reached to allow the County
Council to acquire the land that is needed for the
scheme.  Delivery of Phase 1A is
especially critical for the delivery of a new primary school south
of Barnham Road; the proposed roundabout and school form a
fundamental part of the early delivery of the Barnham, Eastergate
and Westergate strategic development in line with the adopted Arun
Local Plan.
 
As a precaution to mitigate the
risk of failing to reach an agreement, the County Council intends
to initiate the Compulsory Purchase Order (CPO) process
in order
to acquire the
land needed for the A29 Phase 1A.  This
would require the determination of land and rights to be acquired,
land valuations, and negotiations directly with the landowners.
 If objections are received to the CPO, a Public
Inquiry may be required.  It is necessary,
therefore, to initiate and commit the necessary resources to
concluding the CPO process whilst the County Council continues to
support and encourage a negotiated agreement with the developers
and landowners to acquire the land for the scheme.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Economy and Skills (Cllr Garry Wall)
purpose:
The West Sussex Growth Deal
Programmes have played a pivotal role in driving economic
development, enhancing infrastructure, and supporting business
growth across the county.
 
Growth Deals are bespoke
partnership agreements, developed collaboratively with each
District and Borough Council, and designed to reflect the unique
economic priorities of their respective areas.
 
As the initial phase of the
Growth Deals approaches completion, there is an opportunity to
build on this strong foundation. It is proposed that the
overarching Growth Deal framework, along with each individual
agreement, be refreshed to ensure continued alignment with the

West Sussex Economic Strategy 2025–2035, emerging
opportunities linked to Local Government Reorganisation, and future
devolution arrangements.
 
This refresh will also take
account of evolving local needs, including housing delivery,
infrastructure investment, and skills development, to support
sustainable and inclusive growth.
 
The Cabinet Member for Economy
and Skills will be asked to approve the refresh of the overall
Growth Deal Programme and the individual agreements, ensuring a
coordinated, forward-looking approach to economic growth across
West Sussex.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways and Transport (Cllr Joy Dennis)
purpose:
The trees of West Sussex are a
valuable and essential element of the urban and rural landscape,
contributing significantly to the character of the county, as well
as providing other economic, social, and environmental benefits,
all of which contribute to quality of life.
 
The revised 
West Sussex Tree
Plan, approved by
the Cabinet Member for Environment and Climate Change in February
2026, seeks to ensure that the trees within the County
Council’s ownership are maintained, protected, and improved
for current and future generations. Objective 2 specifically seeks
to protect the County Council’s tree stock from third party
development, seeking compensation for any loss and ring-fencing any
compensation to support the delivery of the Tree Plan
through
the replanting of trees in suitable alternative locations.

decision_maker: Executive Director of Communities (Emily King)
purpose:
West Sussex County Council (WSCC), through its
Refugee Resettlement and Migration Service (RRMS), supports
eligible individuals and families under various UK Government
Resettlement or Humanitarian Protection Schemes, including Homes
for Ukraine and the Afghan Resettlement Programme (ARP).
 
The County Council is responsible for
delivering a range of support and facilitating access to services
including assisting with securing permanent settled accommodation
across the UK. Contingency accommodation can be needed whilst
seeking longer term solutions or to manage any delays in moves to
permanent settled accommodation. All elements of the support
provision and contingency accommodation requirements are fully
funded by Government as set out in the individual scheme funding
instructions.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Community Support, Fire and Rescue (Cllr Duncan Crow)
purpose:
West Sussex Fire & Rescue
Service (WSFRS) has a rolling programme of fleet replacement and is
proposing to replace twelve of the oldest appliances, of which the
oldest are now over twenty-two years old and two others seventeen
years old. All having surpassed their anticipated service
life.
 
These replacements will
reap a number of benefits: 
 

Improved vehicle and
firefighting technology


Introducing a
clean-cab concept that reduces firefighters’ exposure
to contaminants


Meeting higher Euro 6
emission standards


Supporting the WSCC
Net Carbon Neutral 2030 goals


Reducing the cost of
maintenance of old vehicles; and 


Critically, reducing
the risk of failure of emergency response
vehicles. 

  
The estimated cost is
£4.8 million (£400,000 per appliance). This spend has
been budgeted for in the WSFRS Fleet Capital Replacement
Programme. 
  
The route to market is proposed
via the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) Framework Agreement for
Emergency Response Vehicles (Pumping Appliances, Aerials and
Special Vehicles). Utilising Lot 2 of the agreement and to hold a
mini competition by way of a tender for those providers on Lot
2. 
 
The Cabinet Member for
Community Support, Fire and Rescue will be asked to agree the
commencement of a procurement and delegate authority to the Chief
Fire Officer to award the contract(s).

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Environment and Climate Change (Cllr Deborah Urquhart)
purpose:
The West Sussex Tree Plan
2026-2030 sets out the County Council’s strategic approach to
managing and enhancing treescapes across its estate and highways,
while influencing development and planning decisions.  The Plan recognises the vital role of trees,
hedgerows, and woodlands in delivering climate resilience,
biodiversity, and social well-being, while addressing key
challenges, such as pests and diseases, development pressures, and
the effects of climate change.
 
It builds on the foundations of
the 2020 plan and aligns with Our Council Plan, the Climate Change
Strategy, the Local Nature Recovery Strategy, and national policy
drivers, such as the Environmental Improvement Plan. 
 
To deliver the County
Council’s three strategic aims of maintaining, protecting,
and improving our trees and treescapes, the Plan identifies five
strategic objectives: improving data and evidence-based
decision-making; embedding policies and procedures; managing
resilience to pests and diseases; identifying opportunities for
investment and improved management; and working with partners and
communities.
 
The Plan also includes an
action plan for the next five years, prioritising nature recovery,
tree equity in urban areas, and nature-based solutions.

CAB10

remain unchanged from the decision taken by Cabinet.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Highways and Transport (Cllr Joy Dennis)
purpose:
The King Charles III England
Coast Path (KCIIIECP) is a new long-distance National Trail being
created for walkers by Natural England (NE) to follow the entire
coastline of England. The final section in West Sussex from West
Wittering beach to the Hampshire border will be completed by 31
March 2026.
 
Once the trail is open, the
County Council as the local Access Authority becomes responsible
for the ongoing maintenance, monitoring and promotion of the trail.
At that stage, NE provides annual trail maintenance funding to each
Access Authority, with an uplift if they are part of a regional
Trail Partnership.
 
The County Council will join
the four other Access Authorities in the region, Hampshire County
Council, New Forest National Park Authority, Portsmouth City
Council and Southampton City Council to establish a new Trail
Partnership to be called the Solent to Sussex Coast Path
Partnership.

purpose:

introduced a statutory requirement for each upper-tier local
authority to prepare and publish a Local Nature Recovery Strategy
(LNRS). LNRS are being introduced in England to encourage more
coordinated practical and focused action and investment in
nature. 
 
West Sussex County Council is
the ‘responsible authority’ for preparing the West
Sussex LNRS.  The LNRS sets out a
long-term vision for nature recovery, priority actions for the
first five years (including opportunities for habitat creation,
restoration of degraded sites, and improving ecological
connectivity). It also provides a framework for delivering
biodiversity net gain, climate resilience, and wider environmental
benefits.
 
The LNRS has been prepared in
partnership with East Sussex County Council (which is preparing the
East Sussex and Brighton & Hove LNRS), Brighton and Hove City
Council, and Natural England. 
 
Preparation has also involved
extensive engagement with key stakeholders, including the district
and borough councils, the South Downs National Park Authority,
landowners, farmers, conservation organisations, and community
groups.
 
The Cabinet will be asked to
approve the West Sussex Local Nature Recovery Strategy.

viability of the school.

section 4 of this report and in Appendix 1.
 
The DfE guidance sets out the stages of the
process that should be undertaken when considering a closure of a
rural school.  Having completed the
first stage, the initial consultation, the Cabinet Member is now
asked to consider the feedback received and approve the progression
of the proposal to the next stage – publication of statutory
notices.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
The County Council has a
statutory duty to provide sufficient school places for all children
who need a place. St Wilfrid’s Catholic School is a Voluntary
Aided 11-18 secondary school based in Crawley. Due to the urgent
need to provide additional secondary school places in Crawley the
school accepted bulge classes in the 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24
intake years. To reflect the continuing need for secondary places
the school increased its Published Admission Number (PAN) from 150
places per year to 180 places per year in 2024.
 
Whilst the school’s
Published Admission Number was increased, additional accommodation
has not been provided resulting in the school now operating
significantly over capacity. A planning application for additional
accommodation to enable a permanent expansion from 5FE to 6FE (750
to 900 places) in Years 7 to 11 was submitted to Crawley Borough
Council in November 2022, however it took until August 2025 for
planning approval to be received, due to delays associated with
water neutrality requirements.
 
The intention is that the
school will oversee delivery of the additional accommodation as a
school managed project. Therefore, approval is now sought for the
passporting of the required capital funding to the school to enable
delivery of the additional accommodation required to provide
teaching and associated spaces to support 900 places in years 7 to
11 and the needs of the expanding 6th form.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
A ‘Sufficiency Duty’ is placed on
Local Authorities under the Children’s Act 1989 (Section
22G). The Sufficiency Duty requires local authorities to ensure
that there are sufficient homes within their geographical area to
meet the needs of children and young people in care, and to take
steps to develop residential provision to meet the needs of all
children and young people in care locally as far as is
possible.
 
The County Council has been working with
providers from a range of sectors, including those already
operating in residential care and semi-independent support
settings, to identify options to increase provision in West
Sussex.  A successful trial of a new
‘collaborative approach’ working with providers to
deliver new residential provision over the past 12 months has
resulted in 2 new children’s homes opening within West
Sussex, and one further home, expected to open shortly, offering
new places to live for children we care for (Decision - 
CYPLS18 (24/25) refers).
 
Building on this success, it is proposed to
undertake a procurement process to establish a Framework of
providers to deliver further new residential units, thereby
increasing the range and number of available homes for our children
in West Sussex.

procurement process to enable the establishment of a Light Touch
Regime Open Framework of providers to deliver additional

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
The County Council’s
Young People’s Supported Housing Pathway service provides a
safe accommodation option for 16/17-year-olds and young people aged
18-25 who are in and on the edge of care and homeless young people.
It enables the local authority to meet its statutory
responsibilities and also satisfies the housing duties held by the
District & Borough Councils 
 
An in-depth review and analysis
have evidenced that current service provision does not fully meet
need or provide the conditions for sustainable change, meaning
young people are vulnerable to becoming homeless and less
economically active in later life. Historically the County Council
has commissioned and funded these services. However, reviewing the
service provided the opportunity to undertake collaborative design
with key stakeholders.  This has
resulted in the proposal for a new co-produced service to be
procured, jointly commissioned and funded with the District and
Borough Councils.
 
The intention for the new
service is that multiple providers will be awarded contracts to
offer supported accommodation for young people at a range of
locations.  As well has having a place
to live there will a package of support services, delivered by the
County Council and key partners to support young people to find
meaningful employment and develop the life skills to move to
independent adulthood.
 
Authority is therefore sought
to launch a procurement process to commission a new supported
accommodation service to provide an effective housing pathway which
prevents future homelessness and addresses health, wellbeing and
economic inequalities. The new services will deliver a West Sussex
wide offer to support children we care for, care leavers and those
young people who are homeless or at risk of immediate or future
homelessness.

purpose:
Yapton CE Primary
School is a 1.5 form entry (45 pupils in each year group) primary
school for children aged 4-11 in the village of Yapton, with a total capacity of 315 pupils.
 
After careful review of the most recent pupil
projection forecasts, it has become evident that a gradual increase
in pupil numbers necessitates the need for an expansion of
Yapton CE Primary School. The increase
is largely due to the significant house building within
Yapton and surrounding areas.
 
It is proposed to expand the school by 0.5
form entry (FE) (15 pupils in each year group) increasing the
school’s Published Admissions Number (PAN) to 2FE (60 pupils
in each year group).  This would create
an overall capacity of 420 places.
 
This expansion will require remodelling works
and the construction of a new 4 classroom block extension to enable
the additional pupils to be accommodated.
 
Therefore, authority is sought for the
allocation of funding required to progress development of the
design for the scheme and to enable construction of this project,
as outlined in section 2 of the report.

school located in the village of Sidlesham for pupils aged from 4-11. The school has
a published admission number of 20 with a total capacity of 140
pupils (5 classrooms).
 
Significant structural defects
have been discovered in a teaching block constructed in the 1930s

undertaken to ensure the school can continue to operate during the
construction project.
 
Approval is now sought for the
allocation of capital funding to develop the design and deliver the
project for replacement accommodation at Sidlesham Primary School.

purpose:
The County Council has a statutory duty to
provide sufficient primary and secondary school places for all
children who need a place.
St Augustine’s CE Primary School is a
Voluntary Controlled 4-11 105 place Primary School incorporating 4
classrooms. One of the classrooms is accommodated in a life expired
modular classroom installed in 1988 which has significant
suitability and condition issues due to the age of the
building.
 
Projections indicate that there is continuing
need for the pupil places to ensure continued capacity for children
of primary age in the village and also within the wider
locality.
 
In November 2020, the then Cabinet Member for
Education and Skills approved the budget required to deliver a
number of small to medium sized capital projects at a range of
schools across the County (decision 
ES10(20/21) refers). This decision included the proposal to
carry out an improvement project at St Augustine’s school by
using the S106 funds identified as being available at that
time.
 
In June 2024 approval was provided for the
allocation of £728k received S106 funds to replace the life
expired modular unit with a new permanent classroom to ensure the
retention of pupil places at the school (decision 
OKD11(24/25) refers). This was in addition to £163k
previously approved under decision ES10(20/21), giving a total
gross budget of £891k.
 
Since then, further design work has been
undertaken which has identified a shortfall in the budget meaning
additional funding is required to enable the approved project to
proceed. Therefore, an additional £580k of Basic Need funding
is recommended to be allocated to this project to enable delivery
of the replacement teaching accommodation at St Augustine’s
CE Primary School.

purpose:
The Council holds a range of
contractual frameworks with providers of adult social care, from
which care can be purchased for adults with eligible social care
needs as determined under the Care Act 2014.  These frameworks are currently under review and
due to be replaced in 2027.
 
In the meantime, there are
occasions throughout the year when adults require a service that is
not currently covered under one of our existing contract
frameworks.  This may be due to the
individual need of the customer, or because the customer is
requiring a service outside of West Sussex, in services which the
Council does not hold contracts with. 
The Council has statutory responsibilities to ensure that care is
provided to all residents with eligible needs, regardless of the
contracting procedures, and therefore in these circumstances, an
individual placement agreement or alternative contract needs to be
arranged to support the customer, each one requiring a process of
approvals for establishing.
 
The Cabinet Member for Adults
Services will be asked to delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Adults Services to award Individual Placement
Agreements until the current frameworks are replaced.

content:
15.1    
The Committee considered a report by the Executive Director of Law,
Assurance and Insight reviewing the process for dealing with stage
two home to school/college transport appeals following changes made
in July 2025 to delegate responsibility for hearing stage two
school transport appeals to officers to deal with an expected
increase in volume of appeals following a change in policy (copy
appended to the signed minutes).

 
15.2    
The Head of Democratic Services reminded members that when they had
endorsed the delegation of responsibility for hearing stage two
appeals to the Assistant Director (Education and Skills) in June
they had also resolved to review the change and consider future
arrangements once the impact of the anticipated increase in appeals
was known. Since then, whilst the expected increase in the volume
of appeals for 19 to 25-year-olds has not materialised, there has
been an overall increase in the number of stage one appeals across
all ages for a number of reasons. Given the pressure on officer
resources and the challenges of arranging member-led panels, the
Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning had
expressed her support for exploring other options.
 
15.3    
On balance members felt that their decision in June had been a
pragmatic one given the anticipated number of appeals and the
difficulty there could have been in finding members to sit on
boards of appeal, particularly during August. They recognised
however that more understanding is needed of the pattern of appeals
likely to occur in the future.
 
15.4    
Some members were sympathetic to option (3) in the report of
exploring alternative options for stage two appeals and the view
that, in order to do so, more time is required to assess whether
the current increase in stage one appeals leads to an increase in
stage two appeals. Waiting until the Committee’s meeting in
February would therefore allow for the collection of more data and
provide a clearer understanding of future requirements.
 
15.5    
However, others remarked on the strength of feeling expressed by
members both at the June meeting of the Committee and at the full
Council meeting in July for members to be involved in stage two
appeals and the reassurances given at that time that the delegation
was a temporary solution. It was suggested that continuing with the
officer delegation until a further review at the Committee’s
meeting in February, and then a final decision by full Council,
most likely in March, would result in an unnecessary delay in
returning to member involvement in appeals.
 
15.6    
The Committee was advised that, following the appointment of
additional members to the Appeals Panel at the Council meeting in
October, the Panel now has its full complement of 18 members. It
was noted in paragraph 2.6 of the report that, whilst the revised
process has been managed effectively by officers, it has had more
significant resource implications than anticipated. The Principal
Solicitor explained that in some instances there have been
challenges in finding officers who have not previously been
involved in a case to hear the stage two appeal.
 
15.7    
Given the previous strength of feeling amongst members, the
Committee supported option (2), recommending to the County Council
in December an immediate return to the previous arrangements. It
was noted in relation to Appendix 1, the required constitutional
changes, that the words after the first sentence of the terms of
reference of the School Transport Appeals Panel on page 22 should
be deleted.
 
15.8    
However, the Committee also agreed to consider alternative options
at their next meeting, as set out in option (3), taking into
account evidence of the pattern of appeals over the next couple of
months and further information about other councils’
arrangements.
 
15.9    
In response to a question, the Principal Lawyer confirmed that
reverting to the previous process of appeals being heard by members
will not enable any appellants who have had their case heard by
officers to request a new hearing as a result of the change of
process.
 
15.10 
Resolved –

 
(1)       
That the County Council be recommended to return to the previous
arrangements for hearing stage two home to school/college transport
appeals and approve the necessary constitutional changes to the
Committee’s and the Appeals Panel’s terms of reference
set out in Part 3 of the Constitution, as set out in Appendix 1
(subject to the correction in minute 15.7 above); and
 
(2)       
That the Committee explores alternative options for the stage two
home to school/college transport appeals process and that a report
to be brought to its February meeting with details of possible
options.
topline: The Governance Committee has decided to recommend a return to previous arrangements for hearing stage two home to school/college transport appeals and explore alternative options for the future.

purpose:
West Sussex County Council

Lodge, Tozer House, Hammonds, Ball Tree Croft and Hobbs Field.

Provided Services (DPS), which also includes the operation of 7 Day
Opportunities sites and the Shared Lives Service.

Services was completed in April 2024 (see Appendix A). The review

significant investment, and not all services are fully aligned with
the strategic direction outlined in the West Sussex County Council
Corporate Plan and the Adult Social Care Strategy, 
The Life You Want to Lead.

residential services in West Sussex. This programme is called
Future Care. It will consider the best approach to take for each
site and those who live there. This report summarises proposals
related to the first of these: New Tyne, which is the only DPS home
that provides residential care for older people with
dementia. 
 
Following a review of this
residential service, the following recommendation is set out for
New Tyne.

purpose:

organisations to provide day services for adults with Learning
Disabilities and/or Autism. The current contracts with the County

reviewed the model of Day, Employment and Volunteering Services and

OKD06 (24/25).
However, three of the lots sought during the procurement were not
awarded leaving a gap in provision for adults in some areas of the
County.
 
The Commissioning Team have
been holding conversations and negotiating with the incumbent
service providers from the previous contracts to seek interim
arrangements whilst long-term solutions are sought. The Director of
Adults and Health will be asked to award the remaining
contract(s).

The Council Plan sets out the Council’s
ambition to minimise the burden of local taxation, delivering the
agreed priorities for residents within the approved budget and
capital programme.
 
The Council maintains
an Asset
Management Policy and Strategy that details how the
Council’s Assets will be managed and developed to deliver

organisations have presented their proposals and terms for
promoting the site. A Promotion Agreement will cover the terms and
conditions on which the County Council will sell the land to a
third party with the benefit of the planning consent.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
The County Council has a statutory duty to
provide sufficient school places for all children who need a place.
The demand for places for children with Special Educational Needs
and Disability (SEND), has been increasing significantly. To
support this increase, the County Council has prioritised creating
additional places through expanding existing Special Support
Centres (SSC) or establishing new SSCs, to support children with
specific needs in a mainstream setting.
 
Buckingham Park Primary is a Primary School in
Shoreham by Sea and, in response to the falling demand for places,
with effect from September 2025 has reduced Published Admission
Numbers (PAN) from 90 to 60 places per year. The School has been identified as a suitable site to
host a new SSC, providing specialist support for initially twelve
children aged 4–11 years of age with social communication
needs/differences. This will prevent the need of costly provision
for these children through independent and non-specialist
schools.
 
The proposal is to refurbish and remodel
existing surplus space within Buckingham Park Primary School to
create the SSC.  Therefore, approval is
sought to allocate capital funding for developing a full design for
the scheme and to enable delivery of the new SSC.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Children, Young People and Learning (Cllr Jacquie Russell)
purpose:
The County Council has a duty to provide
education for all children. To support this, the Council and local
schools commission a range of Independent Alternative Provision
(IAP) to complement school provision, bridge gaps, or support
children with agreed Education Other Than At School (EOTAS) packages. The need for IAP is
predominately for children with Special Educational Needs and
Disabilities (SEND).
 
IAP is currently commissioned through a
Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) which the County Council originally
procured in 2021. The legally permissible term of the DPS is due to
expire in February 2026.
 
To ensure the County Council can continue to
commission IAP, and in response to rising demand driven by an
increasing number of children with SEND, it is proposed that a
Framework is established to replace the DPS. Commissioning
provision via the Framework would continue to sit alongside
placements provided at the Ofsted-regulated West Sussex Alternative
Provision College, which offers full-time education.
 
The Framework itself has no contract value as
it makes no guarantee of business for any provider.  However, the 2023/24 spend on IAP was £18.7
million and the anticipated spend over the life of the Framework is
£34 million. 
 
Approval is now sought to launch a procurement
process to enable the Framework to be established replacing the
DPS.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Economy and Skills (Cllr Garry Wall)
purpose:
In support of Government’s Get Britain
Working strategy, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) have
requested local areas develop local Get Britain Working plans. The
report seeks the County Council’s endorsement of a new Get
Sussex Working plan, in accordance with the DWP guidance.
 
The Get Sussex Working plan will be a
strategic, over-arching document for the whole of Sussex. West
Sussex County Council, East Sussex County Council and Brighton
& Hove City Council have collaborated to develop the plan
across the geography which has been included by Government in the
Devolution Priority Programme. In time, strategic oversight of the
Get Sussex Working plan and employment support will be led by the
Mayoral Combined County Authority.
 
A Get Sussex Working Partnership Group has
overseen the development of the Get Sussex Working plan. The plan
draws on data, evidence and stakeholder engagement. It sets out an
over-arching vision, goal and six ambitions. It also sets out
arrangements for governance, review and monitoring. The plan is
supported by an implementation plan made up of pan-Sussex and
place-based activities.
 
The Get Sussex Working plan is consistent with

Our Council Plan supporting the priorities of a sustainable and
prosperous economy, helping people and communities to fulfil their
potential, and making the best use of resources, underpinned by
protecting the environment. The plan is also consistent with and
supports the achievement of the West Sussex Economic Strategy
2025–2035 and the West Sussex Joint Health and Wellbeing
Strategy 2025-30.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Community Support, Fire and Rescue (Cllr Duncan Crow)
purpose:
The Fire & Rescue Service
currently has a pool of 40 cars, used by officers to perform
statutory operational management duties.  Thirty-eight of the current vehicles are leased
and contracts are either due to expire or have already
expired.  Two cars are owned by the
County Council but are in need of
replacement.
 
In addition, the National Fire
Chiefs Council (NFCC) guidance on driving emergency vehicles is
also changing and a further car is required to enable Operational
Training to effectively train officers in ‘blue light’
driving.
 
Replacement vehicles will be
procured in phases, subject to the market at the time of
purchase.  This cost includes work to
fit blue lights, sirens and emergency communications’
technology.
